note: Every call cycle of the Rust core, which scripts/tools/check-rust-recursion.mjs checks. A bounded cycle says why its depth is bounded. A pending one grows with the input: it moves onto the explicit stack, and its entry goes with it.

cycles.why: Container nesting and content re-tokenized inside content: push, the construct steps, flush, the resolvers, subtokenize and ahead call each other once per level.
Building a block calls building the blocks it holds.
Building an inline calls building the inlines it holds.
The drop glue of Node drops its children, one call per level of the tree.
Printing a node prints its children.
A nested value in the properties envelope is read by the reader of its parent.
Only the document tokenizer owns a child tokenizer, which reads flow and owns none: two levels.
move_one recurses only at a line ending, to the container prefix of the next line, which holds none.
A destination, then its text: two levels.
The standard library's sorts recurse to a depth logarithmic in the length.
